item.title: Google Is Using AI Technology and Camera-Trap Images to Aid Species Recovery | Modern Conservationist
item.description: A new AI model developed by Google is increasing the rate at which species can be identified from camera-trap images, with the goal of helping conservationists make better, more effective conservation management decisions. We spoke with Google Earth Outreach Program Manager Tanya Birch to learn how the technology works, how it is a force for good (but comes with risks) and how conservation organizations can get involved.

item.title: OPINION: There’s a Better Way to Fund Outdoor Recreation — Do it Ourselves | Modern Conservationist
item.description: A bill to permanently fund the Land and Water Conservation Fund is gaining momentum. But should the future of outdoor recreation depend on oil and gas revenues? PERC's Shawn Regan and Tate Watkins explore other sources of funding that are more inclusive of the entire outdoor recreation community.

item.title: Overcrowding and Underpaying at National Parks | Modern Conservationist
item.description: The National Park Service is charged with weighing visitor demand with ecosystem needs, but skyrocketing attendance is posing problems for already cash-strapped parks.

item.title: Black Girls Trekkin' Is Smashing Stereotypes, Proving the 'Outdoors Is for Everyone' | Modern Conservationist
item.description: With a focus on increasing diversity in the outdoors by creating a safe space for people of color to recreate, the founders of Black Girls Trekkin are dismantling the stereotype that “black people don’t go outside."

item.title: Unnecessary Search and Rescues Are Straining Government Agencies, Leaving Organizations Searching for Alternative Solutions Unnecessary Search and Rescues Are Straining Government Agencies, Leaving Organizations Searching for Alternative Solutions
item.description: Today, government agencies are seeing a trend of tired recreationists, without serious injuries, calling for unnecessary rescues. This phenomenon is putting rescuers in danger and resulting in overwhelmed budgets — not to mention, is sparking renewed debate around revisiting the “no charge” policy for search and rescues by the park service.
